clue.text: Centre-forward, he included one in the restaurant

indicators.note: included tells us the football abbreviation holds the word he between its two letters

parts.note: CF is the football abbreviation for centre-forward

explanation.surface: A football striker counted himself among the diners at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the head cook is one of the people who work in such a kitchen.

clue.text: Given preference after being unwell and ugly

indicators.note: after says the word for given preference follows the word for unwell

parts.note: unwell means ill
someone given preference over others is favoured

explanation.surface: Someone got special treatment following an illness, despite being plain.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned synonym for unattractive or unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Chest cold and tender

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid or a resignation

explanation.surface: A patient has a chesty cold and feels sore to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a strongbox for keeping money and valuables.

clue.text: One automatically receives money from it

definitions.text: One automatically receives money from it

parts.words: One automatically receives money from it
parts.note: the automation belongs to the device, not the person: a hole-in-the-wall dispenser that pays out banknotes on demand

explanation.surface: A source of income that pays out without any effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: an ATM hands out banknotes without a bank teller.

clue.text: Frank, say, has wrinkles

parts.note: Frank as spoken is franc, the old French coin, which is abbreviated Fr
has means owns

explanation.surface: A man called Frank, for one, has lines on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks you to hear Frank as franc, the former French currency, whose abbreviation is FR.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as verb or noun: furrowing the brow creases the forehead.

clue.text: Finish set of questions found at beginning of book

parts.note: to finish is to end
an exam paper is a set of questions

explanation.surface: Complete the quiz printed at the front of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the folded leaf pasted inside the front cover (and the back one too).

clue.text: A young animal first detached area

indicators.note: first says the young animal goes ahead of the opening A in the answer

parts.note: a cub is a young animal such as a bear or fox

explanation.surface: A young creature was the first to stray from its territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: an island nation is land cut off from the mainland by sea.

clue.text: Unambiguous copyright Edward completed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled symbol
the forename Edward is completed by the surname of the nonsense poet, Edward Lear

explanation.surface: An unmistakable copyright claim that Edward has finalised.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote The Owl and the Pussycat; 'completed' asks for the surname that finishes his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: plain and open to only one interpretation.

clue.text: Groundwork by graduate with half-sister

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: half, joined by the hyphen to sister, takes just the first three of that word's six letters

explanation.surface: A graduate and her half-sister laid the foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' is not part of a family relation: it cuts 'sister' down to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the foundation on which something is built.

clue.text: With some of the wherewithal, mastered the game

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Using part of the money available, someone learned to play really well.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a board pastime in which pieces hop over one another across a chequered square.

clue.text: Tolerated a bit of banter having obeyed military order

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it, so tolerated is stood
a tease is a piece of playful mockery

explanation.surface: A soldier put up with some joking after following a command.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: soldiers relax from attention when the parade-ground command is given.

clue.text: One quintuples it

parts.note: One is the number, not a person: multiply this fraction by five and the result is exactly one

explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: five times this fraction makes unity.

clue.text: He could be a great artist but he does not produce great pictures

definitions.text: He could be a great artist but he does not produce great pictures

parts.words: He could be a great artist but he does not produce great pictures
parts.note: great changes sense: first it means very talented, then large in size, so this is a painter who works on a tiny scale

explanation.surface: A gifted painter whose canvases somehow never turn out well.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a painter of tiny portraits never makes large works, however talented.

clue.text: Shrubs beneath trees beneath development

parts.note: beneath means under
development is growth, as of a child or a business

explanation.surface: Bushes below a wood lie buried under a building project.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the low bushes and plants that cover a woodland floor.

clue.text: Unjust in the Orient to leave sailor with the Parisian

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
to quit is to leave
AB is an able seaman, a sailor
le is the French word for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: It is unfair, out East, to abandon a seaman with a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: unfair, lacking even-handedness.

clue.text: Rope three initially then another three

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the first word three
another asks for a different arrangement of the letters of the second three

explanation.surface: Tie up three to begin with, then three more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from the first 'three'; 'another' rearranges the second 'three' into ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: As verb or noun: to tie up an animal with a line, or the line itself.

clue.text: Trick Greek character taking seafood

indicators.note: taking says the word for a trick takes on the Greek letter, placed straight after it

parts.note: a scam is a trick or swindle
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Fool a Greek fellow who is having fish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: breaded langoustine tails are a shellfish dish.

clue.text: Excellent selection

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, of the finest quality, as in prime cuts of meat
as a noun, the act of picking or the thing picked

explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for top-quality goods and a noun for an option picked.

clue.text: Double-first of course

parts.note: course is a racecourse, not a degree: two runners both finishing first make a tie

explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a tie in which two horses share the winning place on a racecourse.

clue.text: Be more than a match pound for pound

definitions.text: Be more than a match pound for pound

parts.words: Be more than a match pound for pound
parts.note: pound is a unit on the scales, not a boxing phrase: to be heavier than something, and so count for more

explanation.surface: A boxer beats any rival of the same size.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: to be heavier than, and so more significant than, something else.

clue.text: Showing forgiveness when awful crime's three-quarters complete

indicators.note: awful suggests something in a bad state, so the letters of the word after it are disordered

parts.note: the word crime supplies the letters; the possessive s is not used

indicators.note: three-quarters keeps only the first three of the four letters of the word for complete

parts.note: complete as an adjective means full

explanation.surface: Pardoning someone while a dreadful offence is most of the way done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges CRIME into MERCI; 'three-quarters' keeps FUL, the first three letters of FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: compassionate and lenient towards an offender.

clue.text: Group of performers travelling to Peru

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters of the two words after it move to new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band of actors is on tour to South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a company of actors, dancers or acrobats who tour together.

clue.text: Some of the worst ale rejected was not as fresh

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the poorest beer was sent back for being past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' only joins the two halves: the definition is 'not as fresh', a comparative adjective like the answer. 'rejected' is part of the hiding text, not a signal to turn anything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: older and less palatable than another batch.

clue.text: Troubled well away from the surface?

definitions.meaning: literally, a long way down below the top of the sea, with well meaning far

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for serious difficulty that also literally describes being far down in the sea.

clue.text: Ineffectual sue on manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are movements into new positions, so the letters of the two words before it are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A futile attempt to take legal action during army exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used as a predicate adjective: pointless, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Sexes mingled in Chelmsford area

indicators.note: mingled means mixed together, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Men and women socialising in a part of Chelmsford.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelmsford is the county town of this English county, just north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county east of London whose county town is that city.

clue.text: Wizard place with boat in us mountains

definitions.note: us is the US printed in lower case; the range is named here in the singular, as its adjective and its region are

parts.note: Oz is the land of the Wizard in L. Frank Baum's story
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A magical spot with a boat among our hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' hides the United States in lower case; 'Wizard place' is the land in The Wizard of Oz, not somewhere marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A highland region of Missouri and Arkansas, named in the singular as the adjective for its range.

clue.text: Bird used kinetic energy containing it

indicators.note: containing says the physics abbreviation holds the word it between its two letters

parts.note: KE is the physics abbreviation for kinetic energy

explanation.surface: A bird spent the energy of motion that it held.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a bird of prey with a forked tail.

clue.text: Cat I will amaze going round tree

parts.note: pussy is a child's word for a cat

indicators.note: going round says the word for amaze wraps about the contraction of I will

parts.note: to wow someone is to amaze them
I will contracts to I'll, which gives the letters ILL without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: I'll astonish a cat by circling a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small sallow bearing soft furry catkins in spring.

clue.text: Notice of vacancy when I leave smallest room

indicators.note: leave says the letter I departs from the word for the room

parts.note: the smallest room is a British euphemism for the toilet

explanation.surface: A sign goes up when I move out of the tiniest bedsit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The smallest room' is a British euphemism for the lavatory; 'leave' removes its I.
explanation.definitionFit: The wording on a British sign advertising a property for rent.

clue.text: Games from across the channel

parts.note: across the Channel from Britain lies France, so this asks for the French word for games

explanation.surface: Sporting contests broadcast from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural noun for sports and amusements, France lying over the water from Britain.

clue.text: Two chiefs going round ancient city place of worship

indicators.note: going round says the pair of abbreviations surround the old city
Two says the abbreviation for chief is used twice over

parts.note: Ch is an abbreviation for chief
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A pair of leaders tour an old town's temple.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a building where Christians gather for services.
